title: Ibuprofen Use and Acute Kidney Injury Among Adults Admitted to the Hospital
summary: Among 78,656 inpatients receiving at least 24 hours of ibuprofen or oxycodone, weighted AKI rates were higher with ibuprofen (IRR 1.22, 95% CI 1.09–1.38). Associations were larger with critical illness (1.65, 1.29–2.11) and surgery (1.70, 1.28–2.27); the low-risk subgroup estimate was 0.94 (0.75–1.18).
limitations: Nonrandomized 2004–2017 inpatient data; hypotension, depletion and sepsis were unmeasured. Severe baseline kidney dysfunction was excluded.
whyItMatters: Reassess renal vulnerability before continuing NSAIDs during admission. This study does not establish the risk of one ED dose or justify routine opioid substitution.
evidenceNotes: Primary publisher full text reviewed. Official November 10 publication and release supersede the cache's November 2 hint. Exact-DOI correction/retraction search surfaced no relevant notice; no claim of universal absence. Other analgesic harms require separate assessment.
